newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures lower as brokers eye Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures lower as brokers eye Iraq news.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures eased on Monday, tugged lower by a sinking NYMEX, but brokers said all eyes were on further news of renewed Iraqi oil sales.
September Brent was seven cents lower at $18.05 a barrel by 1435 GMT. Front month August gas oil was $1.25 lower at $162.25 a tonne, just off the day's lows.
NYMEX crude opened higher but by 1435 GMT had surrendered gains with August through January showing losses. Front month August was 22 cents lower at $19.05.
"There is very little going on," said Leslie Nicholas, analyst at GNI.
"London is looking for direction from the U.S., and the U.S. is looking to see what's going to happen on the Iraq-front."

Brokers said the imminent "rubber stamping" by the U.N. of the Iraqi aid distribution deal, the precursor to the second tranche of exports under the oil-for-food plan, was expected to cause few ripples in the market.

However, GNI Research said in a report that while the green light for the oil sale was fully expected by the market, the fact that the go-ahead could mean Iraqi oil shipments in the next couple of weeks meant there should still be a reaction.
September Brent could dip down below support at the $18.00 level, but was likely to trade in the 18.00/18.30 range, brokers said.
